scenes.title: From new customer to their own agency
scenes.subtitle: The operator console and the handover
scenes.narration: This film is for the people who run TravelCRM Pro. It follows a new customer from the moment you create their agency to the day they run it on their own.
The operator console is a separate app with its own sign-in. Repeated wrong passwords lock the account for a while.
The dashboard shows every agency on the platform, revenue, plans and growth, and raises a flag if an agency's calling spend spikes.
Plans and Pricing is the one catalogue behind everything: yearly prices per market, included users, monthly allowances, add-on packs, and the provider costs and margin behind each pack.

A new customer, Skyline Holidays in Pune, has chosen Basic. Enter the company, the owner, the country, currency, time zone and tax system, pick the plan, and provision. The agency gets its own database in a few seconds.
The owner receives a welcome email with the sign-in link, a temporary password, and links to the download and the quick-start guide.

Kavya signs in with the temporary password and is asked to choose her own, at least twelve characters. The onboarding wizard already knows her country, currency and tax system; she adds an invoice prefix and her logo.
Then she invites her first teammate. The invitation goes out by email with a one-time set-up link.
Back in the console, the agency's page shows its details, its subscription and billing state, its plan and caps, usage, and any add-ons. Changing the plan is one step.
Feature switches turn a feature on or off for a whole plan, or for one agency as an exception, for a pilot or a favour. Remove the exception and it follows the plan again.
For agencies in calling countries, the calling tab shows their account, their numbers, minutes used, and the safety limits that stop toll fraud.
The Email page decides how mail is sent: platform mail like welcome and password emails, and the agencies' own mail. It shows a delivery log and can send a test.

Agencies pay online, Razorpay in India and Stripe elsewhere, and every payment produces a subscription invoice in their currency. If a payment fails, there is a grace period and then read-only access; nothing is deleted.
If you must, suspend an agency with a reason. Everyone is locked out at once, the driver app included, and nothing is deleted. Reactivate, and they sign in again with the same passwords.
To help a customer, start a time-limited support session. The agency sees a banner saying who is helping and when the session ends.
Every operator action is in the audit log, and system health and the platform reports show how the service is doing.

scenes.heading: Under the hood
scenes.narration: Underneath, every agency has its own database. Provider secrets are encrypted at rest, requests are rate limited, and background jobs run per agency at its local hour. Test-only tools refuse to run in production. Backups, monitoring hooks and the deployment scripts are built and get switched on at go-live, and this whole hand-over is rehearsed for three agencies by an automated test.

scenes.headline: Onboard an agency in minutes.
scenes.cta: Run your own travel CRM platform
scenes.narration: TravelCRM Pro. Onboard a new agency in minutes, and hand it over with confidence.
